what: HIGH (code audit CA-A10-300, MEASURED 2026-09-27): scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh -- the script every `pull-and-deploy` system-action and ict-git-sync.timer's ~5-minute tick both run on the live-trader VM -- has no rollback-on-failure. After `git reset --hard origin/main` (line 117) and `pip install` (line 338), it restarts every non-skipped unit unconditionally (line 452, continuing past an individual restart failure with only a WARNING) and only detects a bad deploy via a post-restart git_sha version round-trip on ict-web-api (lines 536-567) -- which, on mismatch, exits 4 AFTER the bad code is already live and every unit has already been bounced onto it. DEPLOYED_SHA_FILE is write-only on success; it is never read to revert THIS run. So a single bad commit merged to main (or, per the sibling finding CA-A10-301, a compromised one -- deploy_pull_restart.sh trusts origin/main with no CI-status or signature gate) can leave the live trader crash-looping or down until a human notices and issues a separate, manual rollback. Full finding + evidence: docs/audits/code-audit-2026-09-27/CA-A10.findings.jsonl id CA-A10-300 (see also CA-A10-301, CA-A10-310 for compounding factors). Proposed fix: on restart/version-check failure for a money-path unit, git reset --hard to the pre-deploy SHA, re-run pip install + restart against it, and alert distinctly so the auto-revert itself is visible.
